# vergeio_webhook (Resource)

`vergeio_webhook` is one message sent to a [`vergeio_webhook_url`](webhook_url.html). Create queues the message. VergeOS does not edit a delivery, so changing `message` or `webhook_url_id` sends a new message and deletes the previous delivery row.

Destroy deletes that delivery row and leaves the destination in place. A delivery expires on the system after about 70 days. A missing row is dropped from state, and the next apply sends the message again.

`status` moves from `queued` to `running`, `sent`, or `error` as VergeOS delivers the message. Those fields can change between plans.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One message queued to a destination.
# Changing message or webhook_url_id sends a new message.

resource "vergeio_webhook_url" "example" {
  name = "Chat alerts"
  url  = "https://example.com/hooks/chat"
}

resource "vergeio_webhook" "example" {
  webhook_url_id = vergeio_webhook_url.example.id
  message        = "{\"text\":\"lab event\"}"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `message` (String) JSON payload sent to the destination. Changing it sends a new message and deletes this delivery.
- `webhook_url_id` (String) vergeio_webhook_url.id. Changing it sends a new message and deletes this delivery.

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) Time the delivery was queued, as seconds since the epoch.
- `id` (String) Delivery key assigned by VergeOS.
- `last_attempt` (Number) Time of the last delivery attempt, as seconds since the epoch.
- `status` (String) Delivery status: queued, running, sent, or error.
- `status_info` (String) Detail for status, including an error from the destination.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The `terraform import` command can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vergeio_webhook.example <delivery_key>
```
